77387.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77387.question_text: According to the second creation story, which of the following were formed out of ground?
77387.explanation: In the second creation account (Genesis 2), the sequence differs from the first. Genesis 2:19 states: "So out of the ground the Lord God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them..."

options.text: Beast of the field and birds

77389.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77389.question_text: Which of the following is the reason for which God decided to make a helper fit for a man in the Garden of Eden? For
77389.explanation: The primary reason given is that it was not good for man to be alone. Genesis 2:18 says: "Then the Lord God said, 'It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him.'" This points to companionship.

77391.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77391.question_text: The supremacy of God during creation was manifested by His
77391.explanation: In Genesis 1, God creates through the power of His word (Divine Fiat). The repeated phrase "And God said, 'Let there be...'" (e.g., Genesis 1:3) demonstrates His absolute sovereignty and supremacy over all matter.

options.text: consent that a thing be done

77392.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77392.question_text: Apart from Joseph, who was already in Egypt, the offspring of Jacob that migrated from Canaan to Egypt numbered
77392.explanation: According to Exodus 1:5, "All the offspring of Jacob were seventy persons; Joseph was already in Egypt." (Genesis 46:27 also confirms this total).

77393.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77393.question_text: The name Manasseh, which Joseph gave to his first son, means
77393.explanation: Genesis 41:51 states: "Joseph called the name of the first-born Manasseh, 'For,' he said, 'God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father's house.'"

options.text: God has forgotten Joseph and his family
God has made Joseph forget his hardship
God has delivered Joseph from death
a beloved son of Joseph's wife

77394.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77394.question_text: 'And the Lord said to Moses, see, I make you as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall....' Which of the following roles was Aaron assigned? A
77394.explanation: In Exodus 7:1, the Lord says to Moses: "See, I make you as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet."

77396.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77396.question_text: The presence of God among the Israelites is demonstrated by the symbol of
77396.explanation: During the wilderness journey, God guided them with visible signs. Exodus 13:21: "And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them along the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light..."

77397.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77397.question_text: Joshua's success in the promised land was attributed to the fact that he was
77397.explanation: Success was tied to his obedience and bravery. In Joshua 1:6-7, God commands him: "Be strong and of good courage... being careful to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you."

options.text: carefree about keeping the laws of God

77399.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77399.question_text: During the mission of the twelve spies, which of the following tribes did Joshua represent?
77399.explanation: Caleb represented Judah (Numbers 13:6). Joshua (Hoshea) represented Ephraim (Numbers 13:8: "from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun").

77400.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77400.question_text: Who among the following kings did God sell the people of Israel to and oppress for twenty years?
77400.explanation: Judges 4:2-3 states: "And the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor... he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and oppressed the people of Israel cruelly for twenty years."

77402.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77402.question_text: Sisera, the commander, was killed by Jael, whose husband was a
77402.explanation: Judges 4:17 states: "But Sisera fled away on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite."

77403.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77403.question_text: Which of the following was the major sin attributed to Hophni and Phinehas? They
77403.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:17 records: "Thus the sin of the young men was very great in the sight of the Lord; for the men treated the offering of the Lord with contempt." They were known for taking the best portions of the meat meant for sacrifice by force.

options.text: treated the offering of the Lord with contempt
took bribes and had no regard for justice

77404.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77404.question_text: Samuel was said to have failed in matters of parental responsibility because he
77404.explanation: Just as with Eli, Samuel’s sons did not follow his righteous example. 1 Samuel 8:3 says: "Yet his sons did not walk in his ways, but turned aside after gain; they took bribes and perverted justice."

options.text: could not maintain unity in his family
made his children judges over Israel
made his children to succeed him
did not bring up his children in his ways

77406.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77406.question_text: "Though you are little in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribe of Israel?" On which occasion was this statement made?
77406.explanation: This statement appears in 1 Samuel 15:17 after Saul failed to carry out the total destruction of the Amalekites

options.text: When the evil spirit tormented Saul
During the war between Israel and Amalek
When the sons of Samuel disobeyed God

77407.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77407.question_text: One important lesson that could be learned from David when he spared the life of Saul is
77407.explanation: David refused to take revenge, even when Saul was hunting him. He said in 1 Samuel 24:12, "May the Lord judge between me and you, may the Lord avenge me upon you; but my hand shall not be against you." This teaches the avoidance of personal retaliation.

options.text: to pray for all who hate you
that we must not insult kings despite their wickedness
that no king should be killed by his subject
to avoid retaliation for wrongs done against us

77408.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77408.question_text: Which of the following names was given to Solomon by the prophet Nathan when he was born?
77408.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:24–25 says: "...and she bore a son, and he called his name Solomon. And the Lord loved him, and sent a message by Nathan the prophet; so he called his name Jedidiah, because of the Lord."

77409.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77409.question_text: ... And God said "Ask what I shall give you " To whom and where was this request made?
77409.explanation: 1 Kings 3:5 states: "At Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; and God said, 'Ask what I shall give you.'"

77411.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77411.question_text: The reason for which the building of the temple came into fulfilment during the time of Solomon was that
77411.explanation: 1 Kings 5:4 records Solomon’s words to Hiram: "But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side; there is neither adversary nor misfortune." God had told David that his son would build the temple because he would be a man of peace (1 Chronicles 22:9).

options.text: he offered enough sacrifices to God
his father has arranged for building materials
David was guilty of shedding blood
there was relative peace during his reign

77412.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77412.question_text: A major mistake attributed to Rehoboam was his decision to
77412.explanation: Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and spoke harshly to the people, essentially provoking the rebellion. When the people asked for a lighter yoke, he replied that he would make it heavier (1 Kings 12:13–14), which led directly to the division of the kingdom.

options.text: worship other gods and marry foreign wives
dare Jeroboam to divide the Kingdom
following the negative footsteps of Solomon
lead Israel to war without God's approval

77413.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77413.question_text: When Jezebel decided to cut off the prophets of the Lord, who among the following took a hundred prophets and hid them in a cave?
77413.explanation: 1 Kings 18:4 says: "...and when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them by fifties in a cave, and fed them with bread and water."

77416.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77416.question_text: Elijah ran from Mount Carmel to the city of Jezreel because he was
77416.explanation: 1 Kings 18:46 states: "And the hand of the Lord was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel." The phrase "hand of the Lord" signifies being empowered or possessed by God's spirit.

options.text: possessed by the spirit of God

77417.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77417.question_text: "Proclaim a fast and set Naboth on high among the people" Which of the following was Naboth charged with after the proclamation? He was charged with
77417.explanation: Jezebel instructed false witnesses to testify against him. 1 Kings 21:10 records the charge: "and set two base fellows opposite him, and let them bring a charge against him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him out, and stone him to death."

options.text: claiming to be the messiah and king
refusing to release the family land to the king

77418.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77418.question_text: Which of the following was the reason for which God promised to punish the house of Ahab and not Ahab himself? Ahab
77418.explanation: After hearing the prophecy of doom, Ahab repented. 1 Kings 21:29 says: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days; but in his son's days I will bring the evil upon his house."

77420.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77420.question_text: "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." The discovery of the law book
77420.explanation: When King Josiah heard the words of the book, he realized how far the nation had strayed. This discovery provided the legal and spiritual framework for his massive national reforms (2 Kings 22–23).

options.text: called for the revival of the Passover

77421.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77421.question_text: Huldah the prophetess, pronounced evil upon Judah because the people
77421.explanation: In 2 Kings 22:17, Huldah conveys God's message: "Because they have forsaken me and have burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands..."

options.text: had failed to keep the Sabbath
had burned incense to other gods

77423.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77423.question_text: "But the army of the Chaddeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho." This text alludes to the incident where
77423.explanation: This refers to the fall of Jerusalem. 2 Kings 25:5 states: "But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king [Zedekiah], and overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him." (Note: "Chaddeans" in the image is a typo for Chaldeans/Babylonians).

77424.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77424.question_text: Which of the following ways did Nehemiah demonstrate concern for his nation? He
77424.explanation: Nehemiah’s primary mission was the physical and security restoration of the holy city. Nehemiah 2:17 says: "Then I said to them... 'Come, let us build the wall of Jerusalem, that we may no longer suffer disgrace.'"

77425.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77425.question_text: Then these men came by agreement and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God. The people reminded the king about the following except the
77425.explanation: Daniel's enemies used the law against him. They reminded King Darius of the interdict (ban) he signed, which stated that anyone praying to any god or man except the king would be cast into the lions' den (Daniel 6:12). Freedom of worship was exactly what they were trying to abolish.

77427.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77427.question_text: One immoral act that took place in Israel, which was condemned by Amos, was that
77427.explanation: Amos 2:7 explicitly condemns this specific sexual immorality: "...a man and his father go in to the same maiden, so that my holy name is profaned."

options.text: the rich men took the wives of the poor
Nazarites drank wine and slept in the temple
priests slept with women in the temple
a man and his father went into the same woman

77428.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77428.question_text: To win Israel back to Himself, God promised turning the valley of Achor into a place of
77428.explanation: Hosea 2:15 states: "And there I will give her her vineyards, and make the Valley of Achor a door of hope." (Historically, Achor was a place of trouble/judgment, so this represents a transformation of their history).

77432.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77432.question_text: One significant difference between Matthew's and Mark's account of Jesus' baptism is that
77432.explanation: While all Synoptic Gospels mention the baptism, only Matthew records the dialogue where John hesitates. Matthew 3:14 states: "John would have prevented him, saying, 'I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?'"

options.text: Matthew alone said that John felt inferior to baptise Jesus
Only Matthew reported that the spirit alighted on Jesus
Mark alone made mention of Galilee during the baptism
Matthew alone said a voice came from heaven

77433.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77433.question_text: Which of the following was the sequence of Jesus' temptation according to Matthew?
77433.explanation:
According to Matthew 4:1–11, the actual sequence is:

  1. Wilderness (Stone to bread)

  2. Temple (Pinnacle of the temple)

  3. Mountain (Kingdoms of the world)

77435.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77435.question_text: "I desire mercy, and sacrifice! For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners." Jesus made this remark when
77435.explanation: This occurred during the dinner at Matthew the tax collector's house. Matthew 9:11–13 records: "And when the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, 'Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?' ... [Jesus said] 'Go and learn what this means, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.'"

options.text: he healed the woman with the issue of blood
the Pharisees accused him of eating with sinners
he called the first disciples by the sea
the Sadducees accused him of eating with sinners

77436.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77436.question_text: Jesus' call of the first four disciples to be "fishers of men" implied that they were to
77436.explanation: To be "fishers of men" meant their new vocation was to gather people into the Kingdom of God by spreading the Gospel. This is the foundational call to evangelism and propagation of his message (Matthew 4:19).

77438.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77438.question_text: "I do not say to you seven times but seventy times seven." By this, Jesus meant forgiveness
77438.explanation: In Matthew 18:21–22, Peter asks if he should forgive up to seven times. Jesus’ response of "seventy times seven" is a metaphorical way of saying that forgiveness should be infinite and without limit, rather than a literal mathematical cap.

options.text: must be done only seven times
is exercised when offense is repeated severally
takes place where there is a plea
does not need to have any limitation

77439.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77439.question_text: One of the major things Christians should do to merit God's forgiveness according to Jesus is
77439.explanation: Jesus emphasizes this in the Lord's Prayer and immediately after. Matthew 6:14: "For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father also will forgive you."

77441.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77441.question_text: Which of the following is not a humiliation Jesus suffered during his trial?
77441.explanation: While Jesus suffered spitting, a crown of thorns, and blows, his face was not covered.

options.text: They put a crown on his head
The guards received him with blows

77442.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77442.question_text: "My soul is very sorrowful, even to death, remain here and watch with me." Where was this remark made by Jesus?
77442.explanation: Matthew 26:36–38: "Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane... Then he said to them, 'My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; remain here, and watch with me.'"

options.text: When he was sent to Herod
When he was in the place of Caiaphas

77443.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77443.question_text: Jesus' offer of paradise to the repentant thief on the cross teaches that
77443.explanation: This episode (found in Luke 23:39–43) shows a man receiving salvation in his final moments of life. It serves as a powerful theological example that God's mercy is available until the very end.

options.text: Jesus was crucified to save sinners
people are punished not for their sins

77444.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77444.question_text: "O foolish men, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!" Which people were being referred to as foolish? The
77444.explanation: Luke 24:25 records Jesus speaking to Cleopas and his companion on the road: "And he said to them, 'O foolish men, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!'" because they failed to understand that the Messiah had to suffer and rise.

options.text: women who went to the tomb of Jesus

77448.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77448.question_text: Which of the following qualified Matthias as an apostle to replace Judas Iscariot? He
77448.explanation: Acts 1:21–22 specifies the criteria: "So one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day when he was taken up from us—one of these men must become with us a witness to his resurrection."

options.text: was among the early disciples who prayed fervently
took active part in evangelism from house to house
had accompanied the disciples from the time of the baptism of Jesus
was among the one hundred and twenty disciples who had the Holy Spirit

77450.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77450.question_text: The replacement of Judas Iscariot was necessary because the
77450.explanation: Peter stood up and cited the Psalms to explain why a replacement was required. Acts 1:16, 20: "Brethren, the scripture had to be fulfilled... For it is written in the book of Psalms... 'His office let another take.'"

options.text: death of Judas Iscariot was premature
status quo of the twelve must be maintained
prophesies of the scripture needed to be fulfilled
twelve disciples represented the twelve tribe of Israel

77451.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77451.question_text: "Why did you go to uncircumcised men and eat with them?" The uncircumcised men were the
77451.explanation: This question was posed to Peter by the circumcision party in Jerusalem. Acts 11:2–3: "So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcision party criticized him, saying, 'Why did you go to uncircumcised men and eat with them?'" This refers to his visit to Cornelius in Caesarea (Acts 10).

77453.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77453.question_text: From his experience on the road to Damascus, Saul learnt all the following except
77453.explanation: Saul's conversion was a total surrender of his own will to Christ's. When he asked, "Who are you, Lord?" and "What shall I do, Lord?" (Acts 9, 22), he abandoned his personal mission of persecution to follow the Lord's command.

options.text: persecuting the church meant persecuting the Lord
he was specially chosen to preach to the Gentiles
he could successfully promote his own will
his confidence in Judaism was misplaced

77455.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77455.question_text: "...and there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved" This statement was made by
77455.explanation: Acts 4:10, 12 records Peter's bold defense after being arrested for healing the lame man: "be it known to you all... that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth... there is salvation in no one else..."

options.text: The seven deacons during their appointment
Jesus when he was going to heaven
The apostles on the day of Pentecost

77457.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77457.question_text: Which of the following biblical characters was mentioned to have justified his/her faith by works?
77457.explanation: James 2:25 uses her as a primary example alongside Abraham: "And in the same way was not also Rahab the harlot justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?"

77458.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77458.question_text: "Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church and let them pray over him..." By this statement, James meant that
77458.explanation: James 5:15 clarifies the result of this action: "and the prayer of faith will save the sick man, and the Lord will raise him up..."

options.text: we should not pray for ourselves when we are sick
elders of the church can perform wonders
the prayer of the faithful will save the sick
prayer without the elders may not be effective

77459.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77459.question_text: Peter's encouragement to Christians to put away all forms of malice implies that
77459.explanation: 1 Peter 2:1 tells believers to put away malice, guile, insincerity, envy, and slander. In the context of Christian ethics, these "grievances" and negative traits are seen as the primary obstacles to the "spiritual milk" and the unity of the "living stones" of the church.

options.text: it is a divine command to forgive

77461.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77461.question_text: The call on Christians to live as free men, yet without using such freedom as a pretext for perpetuating evil was intended for them to
77461.explanation: 1 Peter 2:16 states: "Live as free men, yet without using your freedom as a pretext for evil; but live as servants of God." This encourages believers to use their liberty in Christ as a motivation to consistently do what is right.

options.text: fight for their right and freedom
resist the temptations of the devil

77462.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77462.question_text: Peter states that God opposes the proud but to the humble, He
77462.explanation: 1 Peter 5:5 (quoting Proverbs) says: "Clothe yourselves, all of you, with humility toward one another, for 'God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.'"
